Earnings Beat Might Change The Case For Investing In Tutor Perini Stock (TPC)

Thu, November 5, 2026 at 9:16 AM PST 5 min read

Trade TPC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Tutor Perini reported third quarter 2026 revenue of US$1,720.26 million and net income of US$20.7 million, with basic earnings per share from continuing operations of US$0.39. The company also raised full year adjusted EPS guidance to a range of US$5.90 to US$6.10 and reported record operating cash flow of US$331 million.

The construction group reported a near record backlog of about US$20.4 billion with nine mega projects, supported by strong project execution and a net cash position in which cash exceeded total debt by US$707 million. This position gives management room to focus on higher margin work and ongoing risk control.

We will look at how Tutor Perini's investment narrative is affected by record quarterly revenue and raised full year earnings guidance.

Scan for other construction and infrastructure stocks showing strong order books and solid cash generation by jumping into our hand picked list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (24 results) alongside Tutor Perini's latest earnings beat.

Tutor Perini Investment Narrative Recap

To own Tutor Perini, you need to be comfortable with a construction business built around very large, complex projects and a record backlog that can support multi year activity. The recent quarter, with US$1,720.26 million in sales and US$20.7 million in net income, supports that view by showing the order book is converting into revenue and profit.

The key short term swing factor is still execution quality on those mega projects, because delays or disputes can quickly pressure margins and earnings. Legacy contract and litigation risks do not disappear just because one quarter looks cleaner, so the raised adjusted EPS guidance mainly strengthens confidence rather than changing the core risk profile.

One announcement that ties directly to this earnings result is the updated full year adjusted EPS guidance of US$5.90 to US$6.10 per share. That range reflects management's view that current project execution, record operating cash flow of US$331 million and the near record US$20.4 billion backlog are all contributing to a stronger earnings run rate.

For you as a shareholder, that guidance matters because it sits on top of a net cash position where cash exceeds total debt by US$707 million. A balance sheet in that shape can support working capital needs on mega projects and gives the firm more flexibility if any cost overruns, legal issues or timing delays on public contracts occur again.

Tutor Perini's narrative projects US$7.6b revenue and US$483.9 million earnings by 2029. This implies 10.2% yearly revenue growth and earnings rising by about US$405.8 million from US$78.1 million today.

title: TPC Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Higher Guidance & Backlog Growth

TPC Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Higher Guidance & Backlog Growth
Zacks Equity Research
Thu, November 5, 2026 at 8:36 AM PST 4 min read
TPC
Trade TPC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Tutor Perini Corporation TPC raised its 2026 adjusted earnings guidance following the record third-quarter results, supported by strong project execution, expanding margins and substantial operating cash flow. Management emphasized the earnings potential of its growing backlog and robust infrastructure demand.

The earnings call focused on project visibility through 2027, disciplined bidding, improving profitability and contract opportunities. Executives also addressed construction capacity, government funding and the timing of major project awards.

The company reported earnings of $1.83 per share in the third quarter, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.34. Revenues of $1.72 surpassed the consensus estimate of $1.62.

Tutor Perini Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
Tutor Perini Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Tutor Perini Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Tutor Perini Corporation Quote

Tutor Perini Raises 2026 Earnings Outlook

CEO and president Gary Smalley raised the 2026 adjusted earnings guidance to $5.90-$6.10 per share from the previous $5.15-$5.45.

Management attributed the increase to stronger-than-expected project execution and successful mitigation of previously identified risks. The revised outlook retains contingencies for unexpected developments.

Smalley also reiterated expectations for double-digit revenue and earnings growth in 2027 as construction activities accelerate across recently awarded projects.

TPC Backlog Provides Strong Revenue Visibility

Smalley highlighted a near-record backlog of $20.4 billion following $2.2 billion in awards and contract adjustments during the quarter.

The backlog includes nine major projects representing $16 billion in awarded value, with substantial construction activity still ahead.

During questioning from Thompson, Davis & Company, Smalley indicated that more than three-quarters of anticipated 2027 revenues were already represented in existing backlog. He also identified late 2028 as a potential peak execution period for currently awarded projects.

Tutor Perini Targets Major Infrastructure Opportunities

Management outlined a pipeline exceeding $200 billion in potential projects over the next three to four years, approximately three times its size several years ago.

Key opportunities include transportation infrastructure in California and New York, alongside federal construction projects throughout the Indo-Pacific region.

During questioning from Vertical Research Partners, Smalley emphasized disciplined bidding and favorable contract terms rather than maximizing award volumes. He noted that limited competition for large fixed-price projects continues to support attractive bidding conditions.

The trial highlights how AT&T is working to extend coverage without requiring special hardware. This development could influence network investment priorities, competitive positioning in rural connectivity, and future service offerings for emergency responders and enterprise customers.

What Is AT&T's Investment Narrative?

The long term case for AT&T rests on a simple idea. You back a large scale connectivity platform that can squeeze more cash out of an existing network while keeping capital spending in check. Wireless, fiber and enterprise services still depend on reliable execution, stable pricing and disciplined use of the balance sheet. Recent share performance has been mixed, with the stock down about 11% year to date and trailing both the US market and telecom peers over 1 year, which suggests investors are continuing to test that thesis.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

When a heavily indebted company has to refinance at higher rates, every extra dollar of interest comes out of the same cash pool that funds the dividend. Bondholders have a legal claim on that cash. Shareholders only get what the board decides to declare. You can see the pressure at one hospital landlord that just refinanced at 9.25% after its debt had carried a weighted average rate of 5.369%. A big yield often means the market is pricing in risk. It is rarely a bargain.

jentakespictures / iStock Editorial via Getty Images

Here's a quick check: a dividend is in trouble when the right earnings measure covers it, free cash flow falls short, and debt payments keep taking a bigger cut of the cash. Seven warning signs show a big yield is about to be cut, and we list them all in a free report.

Medical Properties Trust (MPT)

Medical Properties Trust (NYSE: MPT) owns hospitals and leases them to operators in nine countries. Its $0.36 annualized dividend works out to about 17.3% at the current price. Most of that yield comes from a falling stock. Shares are down 55.75% year to date, including 24.36% in the past week alone.
